[PAPER_0016, relevance_score=0.303] Experiment 1

In Experiment 1, participants were asked to mentally replay a series of videos depicting people performing daily life activities. Two versions of the videos were used, in a between-subjects design: half of the participants saw the complete unfolding of the activity (i.e., intact videos), whereas the other half saw videos in which less informative segments of the activity were cut and replaced by temporal ellipses.

[PAPER_0019, relevance_score=0.327] The effect size was estimated by computing the mean effect size observed in previous studies comparing differences in temporal compression rates across different types of events (Jeunehomme & D'Argembeau, 2019, 2020). We opted for a between-subjects design because presenting both experimental conditions to the same participants could potentially induce inferences on experimenter demands (e.g., participants might come to believe that memories should be shorter for edited than complete videos), which we wanted to avoid. Participants were randomly assigned to one of the two conditions.
